chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Verily, an angel descends with a scroll at the beginning of the day and at the beginning of the night. It writes in it the deeds of the children of Adam. So fill its beginning with good and its end with good, for God Almighty will forgive you what lies between — God-willingly.
And God Almighty says: 'Remember Me, and I will remember you' [2:152]
and He whose Majesty is exalted says: 'And the remembrance of God is greater' [29:45]

key_terms.ابن آدم: Son of Adam — a classical Arabic expression for 'human being'
key_terms.ذكر الله: Remembrance of God (dhikr) — the broadest form of worship encompassing prayer, recitation, and conscious awareness of God
key_terms.صحيفة: A scroll or record — here the angel's scroll on which deeds are recorded
key_terms.عزَّ وجلَّ: A divine epithet: Mighty and Majestic — one of the most common honorifics for God in hadith literature

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about angels recording deeds at the beginning of the day?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW), as transmitted through Imam al-Baqir (AS) and a chain of trusted narrators, teaches that angels record human deeds at the start of each day and night. The practical guidance is to begin and end each period with righteous acts, with God's promise to forgive whatever shortcomings lie in between. The hadith is reinforced by two Quranic citations emphasizing the supreme importance of dhikr (remembrance of God).

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-`Abbas b. Ma`ruf from `Ali b. Mahziyar from `Amr b. `Uthman from al-Mufaddal b. `Umar from Jabir from Abi Ja`far al-Baqir (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:

An angel descends with a scroll at the beginning of the day and at the beginning of the night. It writes the deeds of the Children of Adam. So, hope for goodness in its beginning and in its end, and Allah will surely forgive you for what is in between – God-willingly.
Allah says, “Remember Me, and I will remember you.” [2:152]
, and He says, “And the remembrance of Allah is greater.” [29:45]
